name: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bank Mandiri: the October print, the perimeter and the discount
frontmatter.summary: We stay BUY on Bank Mandiri with a target of Rp5,670, a 70.8% total return. The bank-only October report shows ten-month net profit up 19.6% year on year with cost of credit at 0.55%, but the model runs on the consolidated ex-BSI perimeter. We take FY2026E credit cost to 0.64% on the consolidated quarterly arithmetic, hold the margin, and keep the call on the discount rate.
thesis: The October bank-only statement is a good print on a narrower perimeter: net profit of IDR46.52tn for ten months, 19.6% higher, with gross NPL at 1.0% and coverage at 244.5% [S12]. It corroborates direction, not the consolidated level, which is 0.63% on cost of credit and 1.0% on gross NPL [S2].

The perimeter bridge is explicit: bank-only loans of IDR1,635.00tn at October against consolidated loans of IDR1,693.63tn at September, because Bank Mandiri Taspen, Mandiri Tunas Finance and Mandiri Utama Finance sit inside the consolidated group and outside the bank entity [S12][S2].
Capital, not demand, binds: an 18.4% bank-only capital ratio against an internal target of 18.0% to 20.0% and a 79.0% payout funds loan growth near 6.0%, not the guidance band [S2][S10].
The variant view is the discount, not the earnings path: 1.1x book against a 1.8x warranted multiple on a 12.8% cost of equity inside the house band, with the base case at Rp6,200 [S0][S2].

The risks we price are the ones the market names: a structural funding mix, a restructured book at 6.8% of loans, and a capital gap that the bear case funds with a discounted rights issue rather than a dividend cut [S2][S7].

catalysts.event: Bank-only November performance report, the last monthly print before the FY2026 close
FY2026 dividend declaration and FY2027 guidance
MSCI consultation decision on Indonesia market classification
FY2026 audited accounts, the first full year on the ex-BSI perimeter
Book-year 2026 dividend approved at the annual general meeting

blocks.text: **Update, 9 November 2026.** Mandiri published its bank-only October report: net profit of IDR46.52tn for ten months, 19.6% higher, on net interest income of IDR67.74tn, loans of IDR1,635.00tn and third-party funds of IDR1,762.00tn [S12]. Asset quality improved on that perimeter, with gross NPL at 1.0%, coverage at 244.5% and cost of credit at 0.55% [S12]. We model the consolidated ex-BSI series, where the same measures read 0.63%, 1.0% and 235.0% [S2].

From the consolidated quarterly series we have raised FY2026E cost of credit to 0.64%: the cumulative charge was 0.58% in FY2025 and 0.63% at nine months, and a series that rises each quarter implies a standalone third quarter above the nine-month figure, so holding that pace completes the year higher again [S2]. The bank-only October rate is below the consolidated nine-month level on a narrower book and is evidence of direction, not of level [S12]. FY2026E parent profit is IDR58.49tn and the rating stays BUY [S2].

We carry **BUY** and a target of Rp5,670, a 70.8% total return from Rp3,610: 57.1% of capital appreciation plus a gross dividend of Rp495 [S0]. The target is the probability-weighted average of the three scenarios below, and the bear case, which is the market own discount rate applied to our earnings path, values the shares near today's price [S2].

The price implies a permanent downcycle. At 1.1x book on a 12.8% cost of equity the market capitalises a going-concern return far below the 23.1% the bank earned bank-only in FY2025 and the 19.6% our forecast produces [S3][S0]. Part of that has nothing to do with Mandiri: in October the IHSG fell 16.7% to 5,057 and foreign investors sold IDR16.88tn net after MSCI opened its classification consultation [S11].

What moves value is funding cost, the restructured book and the discount rate. Deposit costs rose to 2.3% in the third quarter, and the reserve release is a liquidity lever, not a pricing one [S2][S9]. Loans at risk of 6.8% against coverage of 235.0% decide whether the charge holds the band [S2]. The re-rating from 1.1x to 1.8x is the larger part of the expected return [S0].

Bank Mandiri is the largest Indonesian bank by assets and the anchor of the state-owned group, spanning corporate, commercial, micro, consumer and wealth [S3]. The franchise runs on transactional deposits and corporate relationships: CASA reached IDR1,186.06tn bank-only at end-FY2025 and the CASA ratio was 71.9% at September with a loan-to-deposit ratio of 91.2% [S3][S2]. Non-interest income is close to a third of operating income, and the group employed 40,465 people [S2][S0].

The defining corporate event is the loss of control over Bank Syariah Indonesia: the state enterprises body moved the Series A Dwiwarna share to Danantara Asset Management from 1 February 2026 [S4]. Mandiri derecognised BSI net assets of IDR49.42tn and non-controlling interest of IDR23.84tn, retains 51.5% and equity-accounts the stake [S4]. What remains is a set of majority-owned subsidiaries supporting the bank: Bank Mandiri Taspen in pension-linked and commercial banking, the multi-finance arms, insurance distribution and securities [S4][S2]. Minority interest fell to IDR8.76tn at September, which mechanically lifts parent earnings per unit of group profit [S4].

Ownership sits with the state: 52.0% through Danantara, 8.0% through the Indonesia Investment Authority and 26.6% foreign [S2]. Mandiri leads wholesale banking among the state banks and challenges in consumer and micro, where private and digital lenders set the pace; the moat is the transactional deposit franchise and the corporate relationship book, durable but not wide enough to defend a margin against a sustained funding shock [S3].

Indonesian banking is concentrated and regulated, and this is a funding cycle: credit has grown faster than deposits and liquidity rather than capital is the binding constraint for most players. Mandiri is the exception, where capital binds [S2][S3]. The regulatory backdrop is supportive on liquidity and unhelpful on margin: Bank Indonesia cut the reserve requirement to 7.0% from 1 November, while the policy rate was held [S9].

The house macro stance is a conflict we state rather than bury. The deck regime is balance-of-payments pressure and it marks rate-sensitive Indonesian banks, this one included, as avoid, while our rating is BUY [S0]. The policy rate in that deck is 5.8%, held through FY2027E, not the higher figure the sector narrative sometimes carries [S0]. It carries the rupiah at 18,350 by FY2027E against 18,039 spot, with real growth near 5.3% and inflation near 3.3% [S0]. Our cost of equity already carries a 0.95% premium for that policy and country risk, and if it never compresses the bull converges on the base at Rp6,200 [S0].

Deposits are where the competition is fought, and it is a mix story as much as a price story. Bank-only cost of deposits rose to 2.3% in the third quarter while loan yields rose to 7.0% as existing loans repriced, so the margin compressed by less than funding costs alone would imply [S2]. The competitive set is the other state banks and the largest private banks in corporate lending, multi-finance and digital lenders in retail, and the sharia banks where religion is a purchase criterion [S9][S3].

The sector was repriced twice, once for the cycle and once for the index. The IHSG fell 16.7% in October to 5,057, with IDR16.88tn of net foreign selling [S11]. MSCI framed its consultation around accessibility, shareholding transparency and governance, which are index-construction questions; for a bank at 1.1x book an index-driven de-rating can push the price below the value of the cash flows without saying anything about the loan book [S11][S3]. On the five forces, supplier power in deposits is high and drives the margin pressure, buyer power is high in corporate lending, entry is restricted, substitutes are growing, and rivalry is disciplined because the large banks price for profitability rather than volume [S2][S3].

The history is a book that grew fast in its last full year: gross loans and sharia financing of IDR1,849.97tn and deposits of IDR1,816.90tn at end-FY2025, with a bank-only loan-to-deposit ratio of 88.9% [S7]. Parent profit was IDR56.29tn on net interest income of IDR91.57tn [S7].

**The perimeter, stated once.** Two perimeters run through this report and should not be mixed. The consolidated statements cover the group including Bank Mandiri Taspen, Mandiri Tunas Finance and Mandiri Utama Finance; the bank-only monthly statements cover the bank entity, exclude those subsidiaries, and exclude the sharia margin income BSI contributed until its deconsolidation on 1 February 2026, when IDR49.42tn of net assets left the consolidation and Mandiri kept 51.5% of BSI through equity accounting [S4]. The bridge at September: consolidated gross loans of IDR1,693.63tn against bank-only IDR1,605.84tn; consolidated third-party funds of IDR1,804.61tn against bank-only IDR1,762.00tn at October; consolidated cost of credit of 0.63% against bank-only 0.55%; gross NPL of 1.0% with coverage of 235.0% against 1.0% and 244.5% [S2][S4][S12]. The gap is real subsidiary earnings, not consolidation noise; we model the consolidated series.

**Credit cost is the input we raised, and the arithmetic is the reason.** The cumulative consolidated charge was 0.58% in FY2025 and 0.63% at 9M26, having climbed every quarter [S2]. A series that rises each quarter implies a standalone third quarter above the nine-month cumulative, so a fourth quarter holding that pace completes the year at 0.64%, which is what we now carry, up from the 0.55% bank-only October print, a narrower perimeter used only to corroborate that the charge is not deteriorating [S12][S2]. We normalise to 0.70% from FY2028E, inside the 0.6% to 0.8% guidance band, because loans at risk of 6.8% rose on restructured performing loans [S2].

**The fourth quarter needs no step-up.** Ten months of bank-only reporting delivered IDR46.52tn of net profit, 19.6% higher, on net interest income that grew 5.1% against loan growth of 16.5% [S12]. Against our consolidated FY2026E parent profit of IDR58.49tn, the residual for the last two months and the subsidiaries is below the run-rate the ten months set, not above it. Two mechanics explain that without deterioration: provisions are charged on average loans, and the FY2026 average still carries the December-2025 consolidated stock including BSI, so the fourth-quarter rupiah provision exceeds the nine-month quarterly average even at an unchanged rate; and the consolidated base also carries subsidiary profit and the IDR1.20tn nine-month BSI contribution [S4]. Nine-month provisions of IDR7.81tn against pre-tax profit of IDR57.83tn stay inside the band [S2][S4].

**The margin rate is a denominator calibration, not a view.** The printed consolidated NIM is 4.4% for 9M26; we carry 4.3%, because the engine strikes the margin on the average of the opening and closing earning-asset base and the opening base is the December-2025 stock that still carried BSI [S3]. Applying the printed rate to that denominator would overstate net interest income; our rate is the one at which the model reproduces the IDR69.81tn nine-month net interest income [S2]. Operationally no recovery is assumed: deposit costs rose every quarter to 2.3%, the guidance band was maintained, and the reserve release is a liquidity and volume lever, not a margin lever [S2][S9].

**Capital sets the growth path and the payout sets capital.** Bank-only CAR was 18.4% at 9M26 against an internal target of 18.0% to 20.0% [S2]. At a 79.0% payout and a return near 19.6%, retention funds a mid-single-digit rate of risk-weighted asset growth, which is why we carry 6.0% in FY2027E and less after; the capital ratio stays between 18.4% and 18.0% without a raise [S2][S10]. FY2026E loans of IDR1,740.08tn and deposits of IDR1,849.60tn produce net interest income of IDR93.61tn and parent profit of IDR58.49tn, or 3.9% EPS growth to Rp627; loan growth of -5.9% is negative on the reported perimeter because BSI leaves the base [S2][S4].

**Earnings quality: one structural flag, one optical, nothing manipulation-class.** The structural flag is the restructured book: loans at risk of 6.8% against coverage of 235.0% means profit leans on restructured borrowers curing, and migration into NPL would lift the charge without touching the franchise [S2]. The optical flag is BSI: IDR1.20tn of associate income is real cash earnings once distributed but sits below the operating line with no consolidation of the BSI balance sheet [S4]. We screened for provisioning-lag games, related-party revenue inflation, estimate changes that lift earnings and accrual-cash divergence and found none; the FY2025 accounts carry an unmodified opinion with loan impairment as the key audit matter [S7]. The annual report source also contained one reproduced page of external investment research, excluded from the evidence base and supporting no number here [S3].

A bank is worth the spread between the return it earns on equity and the return shareholders require, so the primary method is a justified price-to-book that capitalises the sustainable spread, with a residual income model and a dividend discount model as cross-checks on the same cost of equity and terminal growth. The set suits a regulated, capital-constrained, dividend-paying lender better than a free-cash-flow model, because loan growth and regulatory capital are endogenous.

The cost of equity is 12.8%, and it has to be argued against the house band rather than described. The engine starts at the sovereign yield of 7.4% less the default spread of 1.6%, plus a beta of 0.90 times the mature-market premium of 4.2% plus country risk of 2.5%, which lands below the band VAL_BANKS pins for rupiah equities; we add 0.95% to reach 12.8%, inside the band and above the rate the same book uses for the premium private bank, because that franchise earns a higher margin, runs a lower cost ratio and carries no controlling shareholder that can change the perimeter without a minority vote [S0][S2][S4]. There is no financial debt in the structure we model, so the cost of equity is the cost of capital.

The primary method values the equity at Rp5,626 per share. It averages a sustainable ROE of 19.6% over the first three forecast years, an output of the path above and close to the 23.1% bank-only return reported for FY2025; applies a terminal growth of 4.1%; and capitalises the result at 1.8x book. Book value is parent equity: total equity of IDR302.80tn less non-controlling interests of IDR8.76tn at 9M26, over 93,333 million shares, giving Rp3,147 at the last audited date and Rp3,231 at FY2026E [S4]. Terminal growth of 4.1% is what a 79.0% payout leaves to retain at a return near 19.6%; the deck nominal path is not fundable at that payout without a raise, so the capital-consistent cap governs [S0][S2][S10].

The cross-checks sit above the primary: residual income at Rp6,210, 10.4% above, and the dividend model at Rp6,296, 11.9% above, both carrying the full forecast path rather than a three-year average. We weight the primary at half, residual income at three tenths and the dividend model at two tenths. The published version carried a valuation bridge; it is left empty this round because the ten-month profit and the declared dividend are already inside the engine history and adding them again would count the same rupiah twice [S12][S10].

Sensitivity ranks the levers against the intuition that a long-duration equity claim is a rate bet: a point of credit cost or margin moves the target more than a point of cost of equity or terminal growth, because the multiple is applied to the earnings base and a flat margin converts a funding or credit shock straight into book value [S2].

The peer table is the cross-check the warranted multiple has to survive. Mandiri warranted 1.8x should be, and is, below the multiple paid for the premium franchise listed there, and the listed bank set trades at a discount to our warranted multiples, with the median below book including banks whose capital and credit quality are not in question [S0][S2]. A framework that marks all of them above traded prices is a sector-wide claim about the Indonesian discount rate, not a stock-specific claim about Mandiri.

At 1.1x book the market capitalises a permanent return far below the 23.1% earned bank-only in FY2025; to justify that on our cost of equity it would have to lose several points of sustainable margin or run credit cost permanently above the top of its guidance [S2][S0]. Our bear case at Rp3,532 is that reading made explicit, and the target of Rp5,670, a 70.8% total return, is the base case, not the bull [S0].

**Funding is the first risk and it is structural.** Bank-only cost of deposits reached 2.3% in the third quarter, and the mix has shifted toward related-party time deposits of IDR206.27tn and demand deposits of IDR197.25tn, together more than a fifth of the deposit base [S2][S7]. A mix shift does not reverse with the policy rate: likelihood moderate, impact high, because the valuation rests on a margin near the middle of the guidance band, and the mitigation is the CASA franchise and the reserve release [S9][S3].

**Asset quality is the second.** Loans at risk of 6.8% are concentrated in restructured performing loans, coverage is 235.0% consolidated, and the charge is 0.63% against a 0.6% to 0.8% band; migration into NPL would move the charge to the band top and cut the earnings base, likelihood moderate and impact moderate [S2][S3].

**The BSI holding is the third and the least controllable.** Mandiri carries IDR29.93tn of investments in associates, of which the 51.5% BSI stake is the largest item, against group equity of IDR302.80tn [S4]. A dividend stop, an impairment or a dilutive capital call would hit the IDR1.20tn nine-month associate income directly, and an impairment would hit book value; likelihood low, impact material at roughly a tenth of equity [S4].

**Policy and structure are the fourth.** The state holds 52.0% through Danantara, and the BSI transfer already changed the perimeter without a minority vote [S2][S4]. If the internal capital floor is breached we expect the gap to be funded with a discounted rights issue rather than a dividend cut, and the bear prices that dilution against per-share earnings and dividends with no credit for the proceeds [S2][S10].

**Liquidity and index risk are second order for the equity and first order for the tape.** Three-month turnover of IDR651.1bn a day is deep enough at scale, and the shares sit near the bottom of their year range, Rp3,360 against Rp5,375 [S0]. The rupiah transmits, lifting the sovereign yield, the cost of equity and funding pressure together, with the deck at 18,039 [S0].

The scenarios give the market its own case. The bear at Rp3,532 pairs a cost of equity at the band top with a structural margin compression, a charge through the top of the guidance band and the discounted rights issue; it values the shares at about Rp3,388 before the dividend, broadly today price, so the downside is the loss of the waiting return rather than a further de-rating. The base at Rp6,200 holds the nine-month run-rate, the flat margin and the normalised charge, and the bull at Rp6,747 turns the funding cycle, takes the charge back to the 0.58% FY2025 actual and unwinds the risk premium to the band floor [S2][S9][S0].

The bull shares the base loan path deliberately: no growth or fee shock and the 79.0% payout held, because a faster book at that payout would breach the internal capital floor and require the very issue the bear prices, and at a base capital ratio of 18.4% against a 18.0% floor there is no headroom to lend faster without a raise [S2][S10]. The base carries half the probability weight and each mirrored tail a quarter. Signposts: a cost of deposits above its third-quarter level for two quarters, gross NPL rising with coverage falling, a charge above the band top or a dividend below our payout would move us toward the bear; a charge at the band floor with loans at risk falling, or an MSCI decision that closes the question, toward the bull [S2][S11].

Ownership is concentrated: 52.0% through Danantara, 8.0% through the Indonesia Investment Authority and 26.6% foreign, with the Republic holding the single Dwiwarna share [S2]. That base is liquid enough for index inclusion and nowhere near large enough to constrain a shareholder that can change the perimeter without minority consent [S4].

Related-party flows are large, disclosed and quantifiable: loans and sharia receivables to related parties of IDR402.85tn against gross loans of IDR1,849.97tn, and demand and time deposits of IDR197.25tn and IDR206.27tn each a material share of the IDR1,816.90tn deposit base, with no lending-limit breach reported [S7][S3]. The risk is price risk, not disclosure risk: the state is both counterparty and controller [S7].

The auditor issued an unmodified opinion with loan impairment as the key audit matter, and the 9M26 interims disclose the BSI deconsolidation in full [S7][S4]. The dividend record is the strongest governance signal: IDR44.47tn for book year 2025 at our 79.0% payout and a IDR6.16tn interim for book year 2026, with repurchased shares transferred to the employee programme rather than cancelled so the per-share dividend is intact [S10]. ESG exposures are financed emissions in power, palm oil, mining and cement plus transition finance as the book reallocates; for an equity investor the dimensions that matter are state ownership, related-party pricing and the treatment of minorities in perimeter transactions [S3].

The dated catalysts are the last monthly print on 9 December, the FY2026 dividend declaration and FY2027 guidance in mid-December, the MSCI decision at year end, the FY2026 audited accounts at the end of January as the first full year ex-BSI, and the April meeting that approves the book-year dividend [S12][S10][S11][S2]. We watch bank-only cost of deposits against 2.3% and loan yield against 7.0%; gross NPL and coverage against 1.0% and 244.5% bank-only and 1.0% and 235.0% consolidated; cost-to-income against 38.0%; bank-only CAR against the 18.0% floor; and the equity-accounted BSI contribution against IDR1.20tn [S2][S12][S4].

bear.narrative: The market is right and the de-rating is structural: the funding mix keeps shifting toward related-party and time deposits, so the cost of funds is a ratchet rather than a cycle and the margin compresses below anything reported this cycle; the restructured book seasons into the charge; the risk premium settles at the top of the house band; and with the internal capital floor breached the state funds the gap with a discounted rights issue rather than sacrifice the dividend, diluting the per-share earnings and dividend the valuation is built on.

bull.narrative: The rupiah stabilises and the funding pressure proves cyclical: the GWM cut and CASA growth hold the margin at the guidance top, the restructured book cures and the consolidated charge returns to the FY2025 actual, and the risk premium falls back to the house band floor. No external capital is needed: the payout stays at the level the state has actually taken, fees grow with the book rather than faster, and the lower charge does the work.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs NIM and credit cost
12-month value vs cost of equity and terminal growth

assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is a perimeter step, not a demand call: BSI was deconsolidated from 1 February 2026 (net assets Rp49.4tn derecognised) [S4], so the reported FY2025A loan base of Rp1,850tn falls to about Rp1,740tn at Dec-26E, which is the Sep-26 ex-BSI book of Rp1,694tn [S2] plus one quarter at the 9M26 run-rate. From FY2027E growth is capital-constrained, not guidance-led: the bank-only CAR was 18.4% at 9M26 against an internal target of 18.0-20.0% [S2], and the residual 21% retention on a ~20% ROE funds roughly 5.5-6% of RWA growth, so 6.0% in FY2027-28 and 5.5% thereafter is what the 79% payout [S10] can carry without a capital raise. The 9-11% guidance [S2] is a FY2026 number: the bank-only book is already up 7.26% year to date [S2], and lending faster than retained capital would take the CAR through its own floor without a payout cut.

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: Same perimeter effect: BSI deposits leave the reported base, so FY2026E growth is only +1.8% even though third-party funds grew 4.5% year-to-date on the bank-only book to Sep-26 [S2]. From FY2027E deposits grow with loans so the loan-to-deposit ratio holds near 94%, inside the below-95% ceiling management targets [S2]; the GWM cut from 9% to 7% phased from 1 November 2026 adds lending headroom without deposit growth [S9].

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: Calibration constant, not a balance-sheet ratio: 1.2044 is the multiple at which the model's average earning-asset base reproduces the NII run-rate implied by management's 4.43% 9M26 NIM [S2] on the FY2025A bank-only asset base of Rp2,228tn [S3]. It is held flat because the loan-to-securities mix is stable in the deck [S2].

assumptions.label: Net interest margin
assumptions.basis: 4.33% is a denominator calibration, not a margin view and not the printed 9M26 NIM of 4.43% [S2]. The engine strikes the margin on the average of the opening and closing earning-asset base, and the opening base is the December-2025 consolidated stock of Rp2,228tn [S3] which still carried BSI until 1 February 2026; the 9M26 printed 4.43% is struck on the smaller nine-month average. Applying 4.43% to the model denominator would overstate FY2026E NII in rupiah by about Rp2tn, so 4.33% is the rate at which the model reproduces the Rp69.8tn nine-month NII [S2] and the Rp93.6tn full-year path. Operationally no recovery is assumed: NIM fell from 4.70% in 1Q26 to 4.43% by 9M26 as deposit costs rose every quarter to 2.34% in 3Q26 [S2], management kept the 4.3-4.5% guidance [S2], the house macro deck carries the policy rate at 5.75% through FY2027E and marks rate-sensitive Indonesian banks AVOID [S0], and the GWM release is a liquidity and volume lever [S9], not a margin lever. The October bank-only report confirms the direction: net interest income grew 5.14% year on year against 16.5% loan growth [S12].

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: Fee income tracks the smaller book: FY2026E falls 4.2% because BSI fee income leaves the consolidated base with the deconsolidation [S4]; the 9M26 ex-BSI run-rate is about Rp35tn against Rp48.6tn reported for FY2025. From FY2027E fees grow at 6-7%, a little faster than loans on digital and ecosystem transaction volumes but slower than the 8% taken before, in line with the recurring fee growth management reports and the shallower lending path [S2].

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis: Management lowered FY2026 guidance to 37-39% and delivered 38.0% in 9M26 [S2]; the base case holds 38.0% for FY2026E and drifts to 37.0% as digital channels and back-office automation take cost out, the efficiency path management describes [S2].

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is set to 0.64%, the rate the consolidated quarterly series actually implies if the fourth quarter holds the third-quarter standalone charge: the cumulative consolidated cost of credit was 0.58% at 1Q26, 0.61% at 1H26 and 0.63% at 9M26 [S2], so the third quarter alone ran at about 0.67% and a flat fourth quarter completes the year at 0.64%. The October bank-only print of 0.55% is a different perimeter (bank entity, excluding the subsidiaries) and is used only as corroboration that the charge is not deteriorating, not as the consolidated level [S12]; the consolidated FY2025 actual was 0.58% [S2]. The normalisation to 0.70% from FY2028E is driven by the at-risk book at 6.76% of loans, which rose 93bp QoQ on restructured performing loans and keeps provisioning above the current charge without assuming a cycle turn [S2].

assumptions.label: Other items
assumptions.basis: Set to zero from FY2026E: the FY2025A positive balance is the sharia margin income that sat outside the pack's conventional interest line and left the group with BSI on 1 February 2026 [S4]. No recurring non-operating item is assumed.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025A effective rate was 19.7% (tax Rp15.1tn on pre-tax profit Rp76.4tn) [S7]; held flat, with no change in the corporate rate assumed.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority profit fell to about 3.3% of group net profit in 9M26 from 8.4% in FY2025 because BSI's non-controlling interest left the consolidation [S4]; 3.4% is held, reflecting the remaining subsidiaries (Bank Mandiri Taspen, MTF, AXA Mandiri).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The book-year 2025 dividend of Rp44.47tn is 79% of FY2025 parent profit [S10], and a Rp6.16tn interim was paid for book year 2026 [S10]; 79% is held, inside the 60-85% SOE range, and is the payout the state has actually taken in the last two book years [S2]. It is also the binding constraint on growth: at a ~20% ROE it retains only about a fifth of profit, which is why the loan path slows to what an 18.0-20.0% internal CAR target can fund [S2]. The bear case does not cut it: the state's fiscal need is the dividend, so a capital gap is funded with a discounted rights issue instead [S10][S2].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No change: the 91.75m shares bought back were transferred to the employee ownership programme, leaving the 93.3bn share count intact [S10].

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: Calibration constant, not a regulatory calculation: 0.94 is the multiple at which FY2026E book equity over the ex-BSI loan book reproduces the reported bank-only CAR of 18.4% at 9M26 [S2]. It sits above the deck's raw risk-weight density because regulatory capital deducts the equity-accounted BSI stake and goodwill that book equity still carries; held flat, the model's capital ratio is therefore read as the trajectory of the reported ratio rather than as a regulatory CAR. The internal target of 18.0-20.0% bank-only CAR [S2] bounds loan growth to what retained earnings can fund.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: 4.1%: the rate the model can fund from retained earnings and therefore the cap the house method sets (g at or below ROE x (1 - payout)). With the FY2026E return on equity of about a fifth and the 79% payout the company has actually paid [S10], retention funds only about 4.1% of capital and of loans; the internal CAR target of 18.0-20.0% [S2] makes that the binding constraint, not the macro nominal path. The house macro deck's nominal path (real growth 5.29% plus CPI 3.28%) is not fundable at this payout without a capital raise, so the lower figure is the capital-consistent cap rather than a macro forecast [S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E credit cost is held at the 9M26 consolidated 0.63% on the strength of a BANK-ONLY October print (F72 0.55%). The consolidated ex-BSI series in S2 p11 accelerated through the year (1Q26 0.58, 1H26 0.61, 9M26 0.63), implying roughly 0.67% standalone in 3Q26, so a flat full-year 0.63% needs 4Q26 to decelerate to the 9M average — and the only evidence offered is a different perimeter 8bp below it. If 4Q holds 3Q's rate the year is 0.64% (+~Rp0.2tn provisions, ~-Rp20/share).
challenges.answer: FY2026E cost of credit is now 0.64%, not 0.63%: the consolidated cumulative series rises every quarter, so the standalone third quarter sits above the nine-month cumulative and a fourth quarter holding that rate completes the year at 0.64% [S2]. The bank-only 0.55% October print is cited only as direction that the charge is not deteriorating, not as the level [S12].

challenges.challenge: Every new fact (F64-F78) is bank-only; every model input is consolidated ex-BSI. The report never bridges the two perimeters — Oct bank-only loans Rp1,635tn against FY2026E consolidated Rp1,740tn, bank-only CoC 0.55% against consolidated 0.63%, bank-only coverage 244.5% against consolidated 235% — and it compares 10M26 bank-only NP of Rp46.52tn directly with consolidated FY2026E NP of Rp58.63tn.
challenges.answer: Section 3 and the second thesis bullet now carry the bank-only versus consolidated ex-BSI bridge: consolidated loans of F25 against bank-only F53, consolidated funds of F26 against bank-only F68, cost of credit F21 against F72, and gross NPL F24 with coverage F45 against F70 and F71 [S2][S4][S12]. It states that Bank Mandiri Taspen, MTF and MUF sit inside the consolidated group and outside the bank entity [S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says the base sits 'just under four percent below the annualised 9M26 run-rate' and, two sentences later, that 'the fourth quarter has to deliver its normal seasonal step-up'. The model's own arithmetic gives FY2026E Q4 of Rp13.09tn (58.63 - 45.53), 13.7% below the 9M26 quarterly average of Rp15.18tn and below every quarter of 2026 — a decline, not a step-up. The stated cause of the gap ('we provision above the annualised charge') also cannot hold now that the ratio was cut to the annualised charge.
challenges.answer: Corrected: section 3 no longer claims a seasonal step-up and says the implied fourth quarter is below the ten-month run-rate. The gap is explained by the rupiah provision denominator, since the FY2026 average loan base still carries the December-2025 consolidated stock including BSI, and by subsidiary plus equity-accounted BSI income in the consolidated base [S4][S2].

challenges.challenge: The NIM input is 4.33% against the 9M26 printed 4.43% [S2] and the 4.40% midpoint of the maintained 4.3-4.5% guidance, yet assumptions.nim.basis calls it 'the 9M26 run-rate' and the report says 'we take the middle and stop there'. On the engine's own grid 10bp of NIM is worth about Rp145/share (~2.5% of target).
challenges.answer: 4.33% is a denominator calibration, not a margin view: the engine strikes NIM on the average of the opening and closing earning-asset base and the opening base is the December-2025 stock that still carried BSI, so the printed 4.43% on the nine-month average would overstate net interest income in rupiah [S2][S3]. The run-rate and midpoint wording is removed from both the report and the assumption basis.

challenges.challenge: The bull's credit-cost relief stops at the 0.60% guidance floor because 'the charge has not been below 0.60% in either of the last two years' [S2][S7], but S2 p12 prints FY2025 CoC at 0.58% and the analyst's own new F72 shows 0.55% in October. If the bank-only series is admissible enough to cut the base, it is admissible enough to lift the bull; if it is not, the base cut in C1 has no support. The bull is also only +11% over base with no growth or fee shock.
challenges.answer: The two uses are now consistent: the base cut rests on the consolidated quarterly series in S2, not on the bank-only print, which is used only for direction [S12]. The bull credit relief stops at 0.58%, the FY2025 consolidated actual reported in S2, not at a 0.60% floor that the filings do not show [S2]. The bull shares the base loan path because at a 79% payout and an 18.4% CAR against an 18-20% target faster lending breaches the floor without a raise [S2][S10].

challenges.challenge: The bull raises the payout to 84% while keeping loan growth at 6.0%. With car_est = equity / (loans x 0.94), equity then grows at about 0.16 x 19.6% = 3.1% against 6% RWA growth, so the bull's CAR falls from 18.45% to roughly 17.9% in FY2027E — through the 18.0% floor the report calls 'binding'. The bear cuts the payout for exactly this reason, so the bull should not raise it without cutting growth. Terminal growth of 4.2% also sits 7bp above the model's own ROE x (1 - payout) bound of 4.13%.
challenges.answer: The bull no longer raises the payout: it holds 79% and its only earnings relief is the charge falling to the FY2025 actual, so its capital path is the base path and stays above the 18.0% floor [S2][S10]. Terminal growth is cut to 4.1%, below the ROE times retention bound of about 4.13%, and the bear funds its capital gap with a discounted rights issue rather than a payout cut, so no scenario runs payout and growth inconsistently [S2].

challenges.challenge: No scenario contains the equity-issuance channel. The base case's own car_est path ends at 18.0% in FY2029E, exactly the internal floor; with a credit shock taking CoC to 1.4% and a payout cut to 64% the state can still face a capital gap, and the modal Indonesian SOE solution is a discounted rights issue, which is per-share dilutive to the EPS and DPS the valuation is built on. The bear covers only the payout channel.
challenges.answer: The bear now carries the issuance channel: a discounted rights issue of about Rp15tn at a 25% discount, a 6.45% increase in the share count, charged against per-share earnings and dividends with no credit for the proceeds, on the reasoning that the state already changed the perimeter without a minority vote [S4][S2]. The shock compounds annually, so it is a conservative upper bound, and that limitation is stated.

challenges.challenge: Related-party exposure is treated as static ('large and structural'), but F42-F44 show it moving fast: related-party loans rose 38% yoy (Rp291.6tn to Rp402.8tn) against 14% total loan growth, taking the related-party share to 21.8% from 18.0%, and related-party time deposits quadrupled from Rp53.5tn to Rp206.3tn (11% of the deposit base). The latter is a credible structural driver of the cost-of-funds rise to 2.34% that the bull assumes is cyclical and reverses.
challenges.answer: Related-party exposure is now quantified as a mix shift rather than a static flag: related-party loans of F42 against gross loans of F2, and related-party time and demand deposits of F44 and F43 each a material share of the deposit base [S7]. The bear models the cost of funds structurally, with an 80bp NIM compression rather than a cyclical reversal, justified by the quadrupling of related-party time deposits to about an eighth of deposits [S7][S2].

challenges.challenge: The 51.47% BSI associate is the single largest non-operating asset after the deconsolidation — roughly Rp30tn carrying value, about 10% of consolidated parent equity — and its equity-accounted income sits inside the consolidated PATMI the model uses, yet no scenario and no sentence in section 4 tests an impairment, a dividend stop or a capital call. Section 5 names the governance risk; the valuation is silent.
challenges.answer: Carrying value and income are stated: investments in associates of F82, of which the 51.47% BSI stake is the largest item, against group equity of F79, and nine-month associate income of F83 [S4]. The dividend-stop, impairment and capital-call channel is described with its size in section 5; it is not a fifth bear shock because the house limit is four shocks and the capital channel it would trigger, a discounted issuance, is already priced in the bear [S2][S10].

challenges.challenge: The house macro deck is balance_of_payments_pressure/CAUTIOUS and marks INDO rate-sensitive banks AVOID; the deck's IDR path is 18,350 by FY2027E against 18,080 spot (weaker), while the bull narrative requires that 'the rupiah stabilises'; and section 2 states the policy rate was held at 5.8% where the deck carries 5.75%. The report borrows the deck's NIM stance but never reconciles a BUY at 73% expected return with an AVOID sector stance.
challenges.answer: Section 2 states the conflict explicitly: the deck regime is balance-of-payments pressure and marks rate-sensitive Indonesian banks AVOID while the rating is BUY, the policy rate is the deck 5.75% and the FX path is the deck 18,350 against 18,039 spot [S0]. It also says the bull converges on the base target if the premium does not compress, so the weaker-FX path is quantified through the base case rather than asserted away [S0].

challenges.challenge: The report is 6,948 words (6,666 by the packet count) against the 500-3,500 word update band. More than half is initiation-standard material — business description, five forces, ESG, related-party disclosure — that does not bear on the one input that changed, and the length makes the update's actual claim (a 2bp credit-cost change worth Rp5 of target) hard for a reader to find.
challenges.answer: Report cut from 6,948 words to 3,497, inside the 500-3,500 update band, keeping the update paragraph, the perimeter and run-rate analysis in section 3, the method and sensitivity in section 4, and the scenarios in section 5 [S2][S12]. Business, industry, governance and ESG are condensed to their evidence-bearing minimum.

challenges.challenge: The 50%-weighted justified P/B is applied to a BVPS of Rp3,150.44 that appears as no fact and carries no citation; it reproduces 9M26 consolidated equity attributable to owners of Rp294.04tn (Rp302,797.4m total equity less Rp8,755.9m NCI, S4 p11) over 93,333,333,332 shares (S2 p4), but the report says only 'book value per share at the latest balance sheet'. Separately, the packet's bridge (net debt -Rp27.8tn, minorities Rp8.8tn, associates Rp29.9tn) is displayed but not applied, and if applied would double-count because NCI is already outside BVPS and the associate already inside it.
challenges.answer: Added the 9M26 equity, NCI and share-count facts (F79, F80, F81) and now show the BVPS build in section 4: total equity less non-controlling interests over the share count, giving the FY2025A and FY2026E book values [S4][S2]. The valuation bridge is left empty and annotated, because the ten-month profit and the declared dividend are already in the engine history and applying the bridge would double-count [S12][S10].

challenges.challenge: The credit-cost asymmetry justification states that 'the reported charge has not been below 0.60% in the last two years (FY2025 charge Rp10.4tn on a Rp1,850tn book, F6)', but that arithmetic gives 0.56% and S2 p12 prints FY2025 CoC at 0.58%. The extreme_call justification still says 'cost of credit 0.65% rising to 0.70%' after the base was cut to 0.63%. Both are BLOCK-flag answers that no longer describe the model, and the false floor is what caps the bull.
challenges.answer: Both justifications are rewritten to the model as it now stands: FY2025 consolidated charge 0.58%, 9M26 0.63%, base 0.64%, normalising to 0.70% from FY2028E, and the bull relief set to the 0.58% FY2025 actual rather than a non-existent 0.60% floor [S2]. The extreme_call text no longer claims 0.65% and states the ROE, payout and multiple arithmetic behind the call [S2][S10].

challenges.challenge: CONTAMINATION (partial, disclosed): S3 p.50 reproduces a sell-side page — Verdhana, BUY, Rp6,000 target, 17 November 2025 — whose deconsolidation conclusion matches the report's central thesis and sits within 5% of the house target. The analyst discloses and excludes it in fund record, and F9-F19 do verify to S3 pp.39-40, so no input is contaminated; but the report itself is silent and the page remains in the delivered archive.
challenges.answer: Executed: the sell-side page is excised from the archived S3 text, the source register sha256 is updated with an exclusion note, and section 3 records that the page is excluded and supports no number [S3]. No assumption basis or fact was drafted from it; the deconsolidation reasoning rests on S4 Note 1g and the operating metrics on S2 [S4][S2].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull is base plus 11% (6,946 vs 6,231) with no loan-growth, fee or GWM-liquidity shock, and its credit-cost relief is capped at 0.60% on the claim that the charge has not been below that level in two years — yet S2 p12 shows FY2025 CoC of 0.58% and F72 shows 0.55% in October. The Oct bank-only loan growth of 16.5% yoy (F76) and the reserve-release liquidity (F40/S9) are cited but carry no value.

missing_bear_case.note: Three channels are absent: a discounted rights issue (the base CAR path ends at the 18.0% internal floor in FY2029E and the state has the option), an impairment or dividend stop at the 51.47% BSI associate that supplies equity-accounted income, and any stress on the related-party book, whose loans rose 38% yoy against 14% total growth and whose time deposits quadrupled (F42-F44). The bear COE is capped at the house band top, so the MSCI standalone outcome the report calls decisive cannot be priced.

assumption_realism.note: Credit cost is held at the 9M26 consolidated 0.63% on bank-only October evidence while the consolidated ex-BSI YTD series rose 0.58 -> 0.61 -> 0.63, implying about 0.67% standalone in 3Q26; the bull raises the payout to 84% while keeping 6% loan growth, which breaks the CAR floor the report calls binding; and the cost-of-funds rise is assumed cyclical although related-party time deposits rose from Rp53.5tn to Rp206.3tn (F44).

evidence_and_citations.note: Five spot-checks verified in S12 (46.52tn, 19.64%, 0.55%, 244.5%), S2 p11/p20 (CoC path, NII 69,812), S4 p11 (total equity 302,797.4, NCI 8,755.9), S10 (44.47tn book-year 2025, 6.16tn interim) and S11 (IHSG 5,057, 16.7%, Rp16.88tn, MSCI rationale). Gaps: the BVPS of Rp3,150.44 behind the 50%-weighted method is uncited (it reproduces 9M26 parent equity 294.04tn / 93.33bn shares), no bank-only to consolidated perimeter bridge is given, and the S3 p.50 broker page is disclosed only in fund record.

valuation_method_fit.note: Method set and weights (P/B 50 / RI 30 / DDM 20) match operating configuration and the warranted multiple reconciles (1.796 = (19.65% - 4.2%) / (12.8% - 4.2%) against 1.12x traded), and the target reproduces exactly. But the bull is capital-inconsistent, terminal growth of 4.2% is 7bp above the model's own ROE x (1 - payout) bound of 4.13%, and the packet's bridge (net debt -27.8tn, minorities 8.8tn, associates 29.9tn) is displayed but not applied and would double-count if it were.

bias_and_tone.note: The report is 6,948 words against the 500-3,500 update band, with initiation-standard business, five-forces and ESG sections that do not bear on the one input that moved. Section 3 contradicts itself on the fourth quarter (see C3). A 2bp credit-cost change worth Rp5 of target (5,731 -> 5,736) is written as the reason for the report, and the bear described as 'the market's own case' sits 2% below spot on target value and 7% below on v0.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The house deck is balance_of_payments_pressure/CAUTIOUS and marks INDO rate-sensitive banks AVOID; the bull narrative needs 'the rupiah stabilises' while the deck carries USD/IDR at 18,350 against 18,080 spot; and section 2 states the policy rate was held at 5.8% where the deck has 5.75%. The deck's NIM stance is correctly borrowed, but the AVOID and FX conflicts are never reconciled with a BUY at 73% expected return.

conservatism_audit.note: No stack of haircuts that moves the rating: credit cost is at the last actual, loan growth follows the capital-funded path with a source, terminal growth is below nominal GDP with a source, and the rating survives a doubled bear probability. Two small items meet the audit: the NIM input of 4.33% is 10bp below the 9M26 printed 4.43% and is mislabelled as the run-rate and as the middle of the 4.3-4.5% guidance (worth about Rp145/share on the engine grid), and the FY2025A CoC of 0.60% is on the with-BSI audited perimeter while the forecast is ex-BSI at 0.58%.

calibration.note: The ROE calibration gate passes narrowly (FY2025A actual 19.49% vs model 19.69%, 0.20pp) and all five BLOCK flags carry justifications, but two justifications no longer describe the model: extreme_call still says 'cost of credit 0.65% rising to 0.70%' after the cut to 0.63%, and the credit-cost asymmetry rests on a claim that the charge has not been below 0.60% in two years, which S2 p12 contradicts at 0.58% for FY2025.

signoff.notes: Approved. QC PASS, judge PASS, check PASS (facts + lint), no blocking engine flags. All FATAL/MATERIAL challenges C1-C11 answered on substance, including the bank-only vs consolidated perimeter bridge, the 4Q CoC step and the rights-issue channel in the bear. The two carried FIX items are non-blocking: Q2 is a pure FY2025A dps labelling defect (the Rp6.16tn FY2026 interim is bundled into book-year-2025; forward cash path and every valuation input unaffected); Q1 method-role inversion (justified P/BV 50% vs RI 30% against the VAL_BANKS card) is worth about 2% of the blend and does not change BUY or the Rp5,670 target. Record the card deviation explicitly, or apply the card weights, next update. Rp5,670 rests on a 12.8% COE inside the house band and a 79% SOE payout; the +71% expected return is a deep-discount call, not a modelling artefact.

bias.note: Base case reproduces the company plan (FY2026E NP 58,488 vs plan 57,176, +2.3%; FY2027E 60,000 vs plan 59,959 [S2 F54/F56]) and is conservative on the two risks that matter: CoC 0.64% vs 9M26 0.63% and the 0.55% bank-only Oct print [S12], normalising to 0.70%; NIM 4.33% vs printed 4.43% (stated denominator calibration); loan growth 6.0% vs the raised 9-11% guidance, argued off CAR 18.4% and the 18.0-20.0% target [S2]. Offsetting optimism is confined to CTI drifting to 37.0%, the bottom of the maintained 37-39% band [S2], and a 79% payout that matches the Rp44.47tn declared for book year 2025 [S10]. Net: no directional stacking; scenarios are mirrored on four drivers and each of the three asymmetries is tied to a source (COE 12.45-13.45% house band [S0], CoC floor at the 0.58% FY2025 actual [S2], one-directional equity issuance).

findings.finding: VAL_BANKS names residual income the engine and warranted P/BV the cross-check; the report inverts the roles (justified P/BV 50%, RI 30%) and never says so. The two differ 10.4% (5,626 vs 6,210) and the card weights would lift the blend from 5,935 to about 6,052, roughly 2% of the target.

dps FY2025A prints 542.96, which is (44,470+6,160)/93,333 [S10]: the Rp6.16tn FY2026 interim is bundled into the book-year-2025 declaration, so payout_ratio FY2025A shows 90.0% against the 79% in the assumptions, the report and [S10] (44,470/56,294). The forward cash path and every valuation input are unaffected, so this is a labelling defect, not a value error.

The re-rating argument leans on 23.1% (S3 p353, return on average Tier 1 capital of the bank entity) inside a consolidated P/B of 1.12x. The like-for-like consolidated return is 19.2% (56,294/293,751), which still leaves a gap of about 5pp to the 13.8% implied at 1.12x book, so the conclusion survives but the headline number flatters it.

valuation.post_bs_review is absent (the engine gate does not fire at 40 days from the 30-Sep-26 balance sheet). The October operational print [S12], the Rp6.16tn interim [S10] and the 91.75m buyback transfer [S10] are all covered in the text or in the cash path, but the record does not say what was searched.

flags.message: a.credit_cost: bear 0.008 vs bull -0.0006 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bull moves the consolidated charge 6bp to 0.58%, which is the FY2025 consolidated actual [S2] and not a guidance floor; the October bank-only print of 0.55% [S12] shows the direction but is a different perimeter. The bear adds 80bp because the restructured book is 6.76% of loans [S2] and a funding-plus-credit shock has no observed floor; the two tails are not mirrored because one end is bounded by what the bank has already delivered and the other is not.

flags.message: a.nim: bear -0.008 vs bull 0.0017 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bull is capped by the maintained FY2026 NIM guidance of 4.3-4.5% [S2] and by a deposit cost that rose every quarter from 1.97% to 2.34% [S2], so the most the margin can add is 17bp to the guidance top. The bear's 80bp is a structural cost-of-funds path, not a cyclical one: related-party time deposits quadrupled to Rp206.3tn, about an eighth of the deposit base [S7], which is a mix shift that does not reverse with the policy rate, so the bear has no stated floor [S2].

flags.message: a.share_change: bear +0.0645 and bull +0 do not point opposite ways
flags.justification: The driver is the equity-issuance channel and it is one-directional: the bear carries a discounted rights issue (6.45% dilution, the per-share effect of a Rp15tn issue at a 25% discount) because a credit shock and a 0.70%-plus charge can breach the 18.0% internal capital floor [S2], and the state has shown it funds policy needs without a minority vote [S4]. The bull carries a zero: it needs no issuance at all because it holds the 79% payout and earns a lower charge, and a buyback would be a capital return the state has not signalled and that would consume the CAR headroom [S10][S2].

flags.message: val.coe: bear 0.006 vs bull -0.0035 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: Both ends are pinned by the house IDR cost-of-equity band of 12.45-13.45% (10y sovereign plus a 5.0-6.0% ERP). The base is 12.80%, so the bull can only fall to the 12.45% band floor (35bp) while the bear can rise to the 13.45% band top (60bp); a mirrored 60bp fall would put the bull below the band and break the same card the cost-of-equity build obeys [S0].

flags.message: expected return +71%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The +72% expected return is the arithmetic of a 12.80% house-band cost of equity against a franchise earning 19.7% on book in FY2026E and a 79% payout [S10], with the warranted multiple at 1.80x against a 1.12x trade. The call does not rest on growth: loans grow 6.0% then 5.5% because the 18.4% bank-only CAR and its 18.0-20.0% internal target only fund what a ~20% ROE retains at a 79% payout [S2]. It rests on three sourced numbers held at the last actuals: NIM 4.33% on the model denominator [S2], cost-to-income 38.0% [S2], cost of credit 0.64% in FY2026E normalising to 0.70% [S2]. What today's price implies is the reverse: at 1.12x book and our 12.80% cost of equity the market capitalises a permanent ROE near fourteen percent [S0], against the 19.7% earned and the company's own plan of 19.0% for FY2026E [S2].
